newsitem.title: ITALY: Gucci -- Salomon reaffirms buy, ups forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Gucci -- Salomon reaffirms buy, ups forecasts.

text.p: Investment bank Salomon Brothers reaffirmed its buy stance on the shares of Italian luxury goods company Gucci Group after its third quarter 1996 figures beat the bank's own forecasts.

Gucci announced third quarter sales up 69 percent to $230.2 million last week with leather goods up 94.7 percent and shoes up 69 percent, and as a result Salomon is raising its 1996 and 1997 earnings forecast estimates to $2.50 and $3.10.
Salomon said in a research note that Gucci's current explosive growth was a prelude to what it believed would be a sustainable long term earnings growth rate of at least 20 percent after 1997.
It is forecasting sales in full 1996 to rise by 73 percent to $865 million with net income likely to surge by 66 percent to $152 million, or $2.50 per share.
"We continue to believe that Gucci Group NV is one of the most compelling growth stories in the luxury goods retail sector," the Salomon note said.
The Salomon's research note was first published last week on November 21, following the release of Gucci's third quarter 1996 results earlier in the day.
